payload.headline: AMD falls 8.75% to 534.06; business strong, price still above every fair value

summary.thesis: AMD is growing faster and becoming more profitable, but even after today's drop, 534.06 is well above the highest fair value of 333.38.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The drop broke the prior support zone, and the current support zone is not yet proven.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy at 333.38; swing setup only on a close above 562.99

payload.happening: AMD fell 8.75% to close at 534.06, just above the 517.35–530.13 support zone. That reverses yesterday's 5.86% jump to 585.3. The 546.44–562.99 zone that acted as support yesterday now acts as resistance (a price area where selling has tended to cap rallies). Our data has no news since the last note that explains the drop, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
payload.business: Today's fall changes sentiment, not the business. The last filed quarter (filed 2026-11-04) was strong. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% growth two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 7.1B from 5.4B over a trailing year. AMD holds 8.7B more cash than debt, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts raised next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates by 12.1% in 30 days. What is at risk is how long this lasts. Inventory rose 57% while quarterly sales rose 45%, and unsold chips can force price cuts. The filings risk list also notes that an 18% operating margin sits at the top of AMD's 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. The macro view is negative, with the tech market in a downtrend. We have no segment data, so we cannot say which product line is driving growth.

worth.text: At 534.06, AMD trades at 116.4 times trailing earnings, 66.1 times this year's expected earnings and 30.2 times next year's. It costs 19.3 times sales, against a peer median of 14.2, and sits in the 95th percentile of its own 5-year price-to-sales range. A discounted cash flow model (today's value of future cash) gives 148.51 to 226.75, with a base case of 190.99. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. The price sits above every method. The gap comes from growth. The cash-flow model caps starting growth at 30%, which is worth 187.98, while analysts expect 119% next-year EPS growth. The price assumes that kind of growth lasts for years. Margins matter too: if operating margin falls to 13%, the value drops to 99.12.
worth.key_assumption: The models cap starting growth at 30%, fading over ten years, while the price needs something close to analysts' 119% next-year EPS growth to hold up for much longer.

bull: Sales growth is speeding up: 44.68% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, versus 37.85% two quarters ago.
Profitability roughly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow reached 7.1B.
Analysts keep raising their numbers: next-year EPS is estimated at 17.69, up 12.1% in 30 days, which puts the price at 30.2 times next year's earnings.
bear: Even after the drop, 534.06 is far above the top of the fair-value range at 333.38 and the cash-flow base case of 190.99.
Inventory grew 57% while sales grew 45%, an early warning that could pressure prices and margins; a fall to a 13% operating margin cuts the value to 99.12.
AMD costs 19.3 times sales, against a peer median of 14.2, and sits in the 95th percentile of its own 5-year range, so there is little room for disappointment.

levels.what: Today's close. It is still above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the lower support zone (480.33–502.6, tested 5 times). A break below it would signal that the range is failing, but the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range (high end of AMD's own price-to-sales history). The valuation case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business is improving fast, but the price already assumes the best case. The highest fair value of 333.38 is well below 534.06.

swing.why: Price sits just above the 517.35–530.13 support zone after an 8.75% drop, below the 50-day average of 554.55, and the trend is a range. The nearest resistance at 546.44 is less than one typical daily move (ATR, average daily range) of 41.94 away, so the upside does not justify the risk. A setup would be a close above 562.99 with room up to the 574.2–596.07 zone, or a hold of 480.33–502.6 if 517.35 breaks.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are not close yet. Options dated 2026-11-12, priced off 585.3, implied a 16.0% move by 2026-12-18 and 20.1% by 2027-01-15, so large swings like today's should be expected before the report.

change_mind: A close above 562.99 (top of the 546.44–562.99 resistance), with next-year EPS estimates still above 17.69, would support a swing entry.
A close below 480.33 would break the lower support zone and make even a range trade unattractive.
On 2027-02-02, an EPS result below the 3.3 consensus, or inventory again growing faster than sales, would weaken the growth case behind the price.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait on both horizons. The 8.75% fall to 534.06 still leaves price above the 333.38 top of fair value, and it broke the 546.44–562.99 zone that yesterday's swing setup relied on.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
